#!/bin/bash
#
#SBATCH --account=csc317               # charge csc317 project
#SBATCH --time=02:00:00                # max wall time (hours)
#SBATCH --nodes=4                      # requested nodes
#SBATCH --job-name=pb-imex-n4          # job name
#SBATCH --output=stdout-%j.txt
#SBATCH --error=stderr-%j.txt
#SBATCH --mail-type=END,FAIL           # send email on job completion
# NOTE: SLURM requires an email address to be specified for notifications.
# To enable, uncomment and edit the following line:
# #SBATCH --mail-user=your-email@example.com

# LSF 'jsrun -l' (latency priority) option was omitted as there is no direct SLURM equivalent.
# SLURM's default process and resource affinity is generally good. For highly
# optimized placement, consider options like --gpu-bind=closest. This may have
# performance implications depending on the system architecture.

# write timestamp to stdout
echo "  "
date

# ensure that appropriate modules are loaded
module load gcc/10.2.0 cuda/11.4.2 cmake/3.21.3
spack env activate sundials-demo

# write loaded modules (sent to stderr)
module list

# The original LSF 'jsrun' command requested resources that translate to SLURM as follows:
# Total tasks: 24 (8 resource sets * 3 tasks/rs)
# Tasks per node: 6 (2 resource sets/node * 3 tasks/rs)
# CPUs per task: 1 (3 cpus/rs / 3 tasks/rs)
# GPUs per task: 1 (3 gpus/rs / 3 tasks/rs)

# create srun command
CMD="srun --ntasks=24 --ntasks-per-node=6 --cpus-per-task=1 --gpus-per-task=1 --cpu-bind=core --distribution=block ./primordial_blast_imex.exe --infile=input_primordial_blast_imex.txt"

# echo srun command to stdout
echo "  "
echo "srun command line:"
echo $CMD

# run the job
echo "  "
$CMD

issues: The command is stored in a single string variable and executed without quotes using '$CMD'. This can lead to unexpected behavior due to shell word splitting and glob expansion if the command string were to contain special characters. While it works in this specific instance, it is not a robust practice. It is safer to either execute the 'srun' command directly or store it in a bash array.

inputs.script:
#!/bin/bash
#
#BSUB -P csc317                  # charge csc317 project
#BSUB -W 2:00                    # max wall time (hours)
#BSUB -nnodes 4                  # requested nodes
#BSUB -J pb-imex-n4              # job name
#BSUB -o stdout-%J.txt
#BSUB -e stderr-%J.txt
#BSUB -N                         # send email on job completion

# write timestamp to stdout
echo "  "
date

# ensure that appropriate modules are loaded
module load gcc/10.2.0 cuda/11.4.2 cmake/3.21.3
spack env activate sundials-demo

# write loaded modules (sent to stderr)
module list

# set the 'jsrun' options [default value]:
#    number of resource sets  [all available physical cores]
JSRUN_N=8
#    number of MPI tasks per resource set  [no default]
JSRUN_A=3
#    number of CPUs per resource set  [1]
JSRUN_C=3
#    number of GPUs per resource set  [0]
JSRUN_G=3
#    binding of tasks within a resource set (none / rs / packed:#)  [packed:1]
JSRUN_B=packed:1
#    number of resource sets per host  [no default]
JSRUN_R=2
#    latency priority (CPU-CPU / GPU-CPU)  [GPU-CPU,CPU-MEM,CPU-CPU]
JSRUN_L=GPU-CPU
#    how tasks are started on resource sets  [packed]
JSRUN_D=packed

# create jsrun command
CMD="jsrun -n $JSRUN_N -a $JSRUN_A -c $JSRUN_C -g $JSRUN_G -b $JSRUN_B -r $JSRUN_R -l $JSRUN_L -d $JSRUN_D ./primordial_blast_imex.exe --infile=input_primordial_blast_imex.txt"

# echo jsrun command to stdout
echo "  "
echo "jsrun command line:"
echo $CMD

# run the job
echo "  "
$CMD
